REPORT ON John Rasordovitch.
Made by D.S.I. Sullivan. Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.
Sir,
Enquiries have been made but no trace can be found of a man named John Rasordovitch. The manager of the Burlington Hotel states that he has never known a Korean to stay or dine at the hotel during the time he has been there (over two years).
There is a man named John Liserovitch staying at No. 1 Young Allen Terrace which is just off Beme Road. Lizerovitch and his friend, a man named A. Levenspeil are both Russians who were brought up in England and speak English fluently.
They have been in Shanghai about 15 months and during that time there has been no cause to suspect Lizerovitch. His companion, Levenspeil, however has been the subject of enquiries on two or three occasions.
It is possible that a mistake has been made in the spelling or pronunciation of the name and that Liserovitch is the man whose whereabouts are sought.
Previous reports attached.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Mr. Johnson states that the locality is purely Chinese and taking into consideration the well-known antipathy of the Chinese to living in premises situated on wide roads, is of opinion that a road of 80 ft. in width will be detrimental to the new premises about to be erected. He does not agree that the same terms as were accepted in the cases of Lots 694 and 694a are applicable to Lot 1325, as the Cemetery Road afforded ample access.
He refers to a previous instance where the Council acknowledged there was no betterment where roads were over 30 feet wide and he contends that the new road was for the benefit of the public only and not for property owners. The Assistant Secretary replies that in the case referred to the land was situated in a Chinese locality. Mr. Johnson states that in 1916, Lot 1325 was re-assessed at 43 per cent. higher and other lots in the vicinity only from 9½ to 17 per cent. higher, showing that the owners of this lot were already contributing towards the filling in of the creek, by having been so assessed; so he does not see why Lot 1325 should be reduced in area unless at the assessed value plus 10 per cent. for compulsory surrender.
To this the Assistant Secretary submits that the admission that the lot is assessed 43 per cent. higher, as against 9½ per cent. to 17 per cent. higher for neighbouring properties, proves the Council's point that the project for conversion of a pestilential creek into a broad thoroughfare has enormously improved the value of the lot under discussion; and further that it is no valid argument to suggest that payment of land tax at the enhanced rate, i.e., six-tenths of one per cent. per annum, has relieved the owners from the obligation to co-operate by a capital contribution in the public work which so much enhances the value of their land.

Sir,

A. Levenspeil came to Shanghai from Vladivostock together with one J. Lezerovitch on March 1st last.

Both men are said to have been taken to England when they were infants, and to have left London to join the Russian Army. On arriving in Russia the revolution was in full swing, so they came to Shanghai.

Levenspeil is a rather well educated man, having studied for some time at the London University. He has a good theoretical knowledge, but not much practical knowledge, of engineering. He speaks English fluently, is said to have strong socialistic opinions, and associates with Russians.

He is employed at present in the Shanghai Tramway Co. as an assistant to the Line Engineer.

He formerly lived at the Hanbury Institute, but has now removed to 52 Temple Lane, where he lives with a Mr. Tobias, Manager of N. Lazarus, optician, 12 Nanking Road.

He is a stout, sturdily built, clean shaven, rather dark man, about 20 years old.

His companion J. Lezerovitch is a man of much quieter temperament. Lives at the Hanbury Institute and is employed in the Insurance Department of Messrs Jardine, Matheson & Co.

关于迈克尔·多尔（Michael Doll）的报告。

由警佐沙利文（D.S. Sullivan）撰写。呈报

阁下，

迈克尔·多尔系俄裔入籍加拿大人。

他于前些年首次来到中国，并在广州加入海关。被解职后，他于1917年初来到上海，以多尔特（Dolt）之名加入水上巡捕队。当海关当局查明其真实身份后，他在水上巡捕队任职约4个月即被解职。

此后，他曾受雇于轮船招商局，但仅停留数月。

他数次入住汉伯里研究所（Hanbury Institute），该所管理人因伍德先生（Mr. Inwood）称，多尔曾试图获取前往符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）的护照，但未能找到人在其申请上签字。

数月来，多尔未从事任何固定工作。他在符拉迪沃斯托克、首尔（Seoul）及其他北方港口与上海之间往返。他目前住在四川路大陆饭店（Continental Hotel），并打算在数日后乘坐“奔萨”号轮船（s.s. Penza）前往符拉迪沃斯托克。

他谈论买卖糖精之事，但据查，他实际上从未进行过此类商品的任何交易。

多尔外貌身高约5英尺11英寸，体格健壮，年约30岁，面部无须，外表显得非常散漫，总体看来较为粗鲁。
